metadata.rules_text:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes or volatility; apply downward bias correction for first 5–7 days post-event.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits strong mean-reversion bias — forecasts drift toward historical averages too quickly; adjust by adding 10–15% lagged volatility buffer.
- After a price spike (e.g., >15% above recent mean), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 5–10% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- In low-sentiment environments, model tends to ignore downward momentum; if true outcome shows sustained decline, add 5–8% downward adjustment to next 7-day forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently fails to capture late-cycle corrections; if true outcome shows sharp drop in final 5–7 days, apply “tail correction” — reduce final 3–5 days by 5–10% to align with observed mean reversion.
